name: Cuba
sources: CUBA HAS NO HONEST DOLLAR GDP FOR 1990 AND THIS FILE SHOULD NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE. Cuba reported Global Social Product on the Soviet material-product system, not GDP, and converted at an administrative one-peso-to-one-dollar rate. The World Bank carries $28.645bn for 1990 on that official rate, and $28.6bn is the figure entered here for consistency with the rest of the roster; contemporary CIA and academic estimates using purchasing-power or shadow rates run from roughly $15bn to $30bn for the same year. Population 10.6m is solid (ONE, 1990).

TFP trend -1.2%/yr: Soviet trade subsidies, which had been running at roughly a quarter of Cuban GNP through sugar priced far above the world market and oil priced below it, were being withdrawn as the CMEA settlement moved to hard currency from January 1991. The Periodo Especial en Tiempo de Paz is declared in August 1990. Output falls about 35% over the following four years — the model has to produce that from the loss of the patron, not from a date.

Inflation 0.02 and interest_rate 0.045 are administered, not market, figures. Cuban prices were fixed and the real phenomenon was a monetary overhang estimated at 4 to 5 billion pesos of forced saving against empty shops; there is no market rate to transcribe.

Tax take 55% and state investment 16% of GDP: on the command-economy convention the state budget absorbs and reallocates most of output. Private investment 0.01 — self-employment was not legalised again until September 1993.

Debt 0.55: convertible-currency debt about $6.2bn at end-1990, in default and unserviced since the 1986 suspension, plus roughly 15-20bn transferable roubles owed to the Soviet Union whose dollar value has never been agreed by either side. That second figure is why this row is a judgement and is flagged as one.
Oil 0.018 mbd: domestic production about 18,000 bbl/d of heavy crude, against imports from the USSR of some 200,000-300,000 bbl/d that were the true energy base and that stop arriving in 1991-92.

Defence 6% of GDP and strength 12: the FAR were the largest and most combat-experienced force in Latin America, having fought in Angola from 1975 until the last troops came home in May 1991, and in Ethiopia. Strength sits well above what the economy buys anyone else, on the same grounds as Israel's does.

Stability 58 and separatism 0.0: the regime was institutionally solid — no ethnic or regional cleavage at all — but 1989 had brought the trial and execution of General Arnaldo Ochoa, a Hero of the Republic, in July, and the patron was visibly dying. authoritarianism 0.92 sits above the electoral ceiling: National Assembly deputies were chosen indirectly by municipal assemblies until the 1993 reform, and there was one legal party.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.8970%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series CUB (Cuba): 10,073,299 in 1984 to 10,533,243 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: CUB.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 92% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: bio_universal_immunisation GRANTED.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 0 against a threshold of any positive count: refused.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 immunisation coverage (% of surviving infants), retrieved from the UNICEF public SDMX API, dataflow UNICEF:IMMUNISATION(1.0), indicator IM_DTP3, DATA_SOURCE field 'WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage, 2025 revision'. Series value: CUB, 1990 = 92%, at or above the 80% WHO/UNICEF Universal Childhood Immunization (UCI-1990) target that defines this technology's name.
